quote.text: the heptazethrene derivative HZ-TIPS has a closed-shell ground state

In contrast to our previously reported open-shell heptazethrene diimide (HZ-DI),17 the HZ-TIPS has a closed-shell ground state, although it has the same heptazethrene core. This can be explained by the relatively large energy gap of the latter, indicating that a small energy gap is crucial for an open-shell ground state structure.

exp.value: “While HZ-TIPS was predicted to have some lower degree of singlet biradical character in the ground state, our experimental data suggested its closed-shell electronic structure. Such difference between theory and experiment has been observed for other PAHs, especially for those having borderline biradical characters.”

“Interestingly, it was found that HZ-TIPS behaves like a typical closed-shell PAH (such as zethrene), different from the HZ-DI with the same heptazethrene core. Such a difference can be explained by the relatively small HOMO–LUMO energy gap of HZ-DI (0.99 eV) compared to HZ-TIPS (1.47 eV). That is, the large energy gap in HZ-TIPS makes the admixing of HOMO and LUMO in the ground state less efficient, and thus leads to smaller diradical character.”
“a derivative, 2, with methyl and silylethynyl substituents at the 1,9- and 7,15-positions has been reported as the first closed-shell congener (Li et al., 2012).”

wording.quote: in the singlet diradical ground state

Although our original intention is to synthesize stable compounds with significant tetraradical character, all four systems we studied should be better described as diradicaloids because the tetraradical characters are substantially small.
It turned out that the fusion mode has a dramatic effect on the ground-state electronic structures, diradical character and tetraradical characters, and chemical reactivity.

The HZ dimer HZD has a large diradical character and is highly reactive and gave dioxo-product upon contact with air. Upon introducing two cyclopenta rings in FP and PIF, the diradical character greatly decreases.
Because of unbalanced radical−radical interactions, these compounds exhibited small tetraradical character and are better described as diradicaloids with tunable diradical character.
Open-shell singlet diradicaloids display unique electronic, nonlinear optical, and magnetic activity and could become novel molecular materials for organic electronics, photonics, and spintronics.

wording.scope: the seven systems of the paper
wording.quote: It was found that their diradical and tetraradical characters show a clear dependence on the fusion mode. Upon the introduction of more five-membered rings, the diradical characters greatly decrease.

wording.scope: PHs with an open-shell singlet diradical ground state
wording.quote: π-Conjugated polycyclic hydrocarbons (PHs) with an open-shell singlet diradical ground state have recently attracted tremendous interest due to their unique electronic, optical, and magnetic properties and potential applications in organic electronics, nonlinear optics, spintronics, and energy storage devices.

The next natural target is to access stable open-shell singlet tetraradicaloids or even polyradicaloids, which may open the opportunities to investigate multiple spin interactions and molecular magnetism.
One of the most important discoveries for this type of molecule is their open-shell diradical character, which is the origin of their unique optical, electronic, and magnetic properties.

So far, most reported extended zethrene molecules have a singlet diradical ground state. The next natural target is to access stable zethrene-based tetraradicaloids or even polyradicaloids, which may open opportunities to investigate multiple spin interactions and molecular magnetism.
This was the first time that we revealed the unique open-shell singlet ground state for higher order zethrenes

The discovery of the open-shell diradial character of extended zethrenes is of importance as it explains why all previous attempts were not so successful, and it also opens the door to approach many other stable open-shell singlet diradicaloids and polyradicalids.15

They display unique magnetic activity due to the small singlet-triplet energy gap. ... lukman.quote: We note that the observed phosphorescence contrasts with energies estimated from temperature-dependent SQUID measurements,35,38 which generally suggest E(T1) < ∼200 meV. The long triplet lifetimes we measure in solution sensitization experiments (Supplementary Figures 2 and 4−8) and porphyrin-sensitized phosphorescence spectra cannot be reconciled with such low triplet energies. Our comprehensive spectroscopic study here can only be rationalized in terms of these markedly higher triplet energies, measured with the most direct method available, and we suggest that the earlier measurements reflected charged species rather than excitonic triplets, as suggested by ESR measurements.47
